2. The journey, step by step

Each step is pictured as it happened: a screenshot of the Inkcast page the person saw, or a panel rendering the MCP tool call or REST request the client made and the reply it got. The line under each picture is what the step checked; a check that fails fails the step. A page with a JavaScript error, an HTTP error status or a visible error is refused rather than pictured as a success.

1. Add Inkcast to an MCP client

Step 1 — REST — GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp (rest, 2026-10-22T07:12:13Z)

The client asks the MCP endpoint who protects it: Inkcast's own authorization server.

✓ HTTP 200; the resource names its authorization server

Step 2 — REST — GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (rest, 2026-10-22T07:12:13Z)

Discovery: where to register, authorize and get tokens; PKCE S256 is required.

✓ HTTP 200; metadata lists registration, authorization and token endpoints with S256

Step 3 — dynamic client registration (mcp, 2026-10-22T07:12:14Z)

The client registered itself (RFC 7591); no secret, PKCE instead.

✓ registered as “Walkthrough MCP client” (client_id 157d7408-6877-4ec2-b18d-6b3b4d28c78b), redirect http://localhost:53682/callback

Step 4 — sign-in page (browser, 2026-10-22T07:12:15Z)

The client opened the authorization URL in the browser; Inkcast asks the person to sign in.

✓ http://localhost:8787/auth/login?pending=Rdty5sAXO9lxzEdYsZLi6dQQruEY3Ec- — Sign in; the sign-in form

Step 5 — consent page (browser, 2026-10-22T07:12:15Z)

Signed in: Inkcast asks whether this client may use the account, naming the client.

✓ http://localhost:8787/auth/consent?pending=Rdty5sAXO9lxzEdYsZLi6dQQruEY3Ec- — Allow Walkthrough MCP client to use Inkcast?; consent names the client

Step 6 — authorization code at the local callback (check, 2026-10-22T07:12:15Z)

The browser was sent back to the client's local listener with a one-time code; the client exchanges it with its PKCE verifier.

✓ the redirect reached http://localhost:53682/callback with a code and state

Step 7 — token exchange (mcp, 2026-10-22T07:12:15Z)

The code and verifier became an access token and a refresh token; the client stores them.

✓ access token issued, expires in 3600 s, scope: inkcast

Step 8 — MCP initialize (mcp, 2026-10-22T07:12:16Z)

The session is open: the server introduces itself and lists its tools.

✓ server “inkcast” 0.1.0; 9 tools: inkcast_platforms, inkcast_connect, inkcast_disconnect, inkcast_destinations, inkcast_publish, inkcast_sync, inkcast_posts, inkcast_cancel, inkcast_create_token

6. Git sync, as the GitHub Action does it

Step 25 — REST — POST /api/v1/stories:sync (rest, 2026-10-22T07:12:20Z)

What the GitHub Action sends on a push: the file, its path and the repository id, with the personal access token and an Idempotency-Key so a retried job can never publish twice.

✓ HTTP 200; the file was created on DEV with a URL

Step 26 — REST — GET /api/v1/ledger?source=github.com/acme/blog (rest, 2026-10-22T07:12:20Z)

The ledger: what each file became on each platform, keyed by the hash of what was sent.

✓ HTTP 200; the ledger has the file, published, with a content hash

7. Insights
